"He said he'd been in the Navy and, you know, I was looking for a strong guy to represent to my sons what I thought they needed to be," Allen said. outputs.L1:
(CNN) — With his hands and feet shackled and his face obscured by long hair, Chester Arthur Stiles made his initial court appearance Wednesday morning in Las Vegas, Nevada, on charges stemming from the videotaped rape of a 2-year-old girl.

Stiles, 37, appeared in a Las Vegas courtroom after being taken into custody Monday night, when a Henderson, Nevada, police officer pulled over the white Buick Century he was driving.

Before Wednesday’s hearing, prosecutors added several charges, bringing the total to 23 felony counts. The charges include lewdness with a minor, sexual assault, and use of a child in the production of pornography, according to a statement issued by the Clark County, Nevada, court. One lewdness charge stems from a 2004 incident, while the remaining charges are related to the videotape, the court said.

Judge Deborah Lippis set a preliminary hearing for November 19.

After the hearing, Stiles’ court-appointed attorney said his client appeared overwhelmed by public opinion surrounding the case.

“I think he’s a little out of it,” public defender Jeff Banks said.

Jerry T. Donohue, the attorney for the girl’s mother, told CNN that the child seen in the videotape was younger than 3 when the abuse occurred. The girl, now 7, was located last month following a nationwide search.

The girl’s mother said Wednesday on “The Dr. Phil Show” that she was “relieved” by Stiles’ arrest, although she added that it would have been “better if they found him dead.” She said she would testify against Stiles if the case goes to court.

She told Phil McGraw that her daughter has no memory of the videotaped assault and that she recently spoke with the girl about inappropriate touching. According to the mother, her daughter said that if someone touched her inappropriately, she would scream and tell her mother.

But, the mother told McGraw, “I don’t trust anybody now.” Although she is in a relationship with a man her daughter calls “Dad,” she said, “I don’t feel comfortable leaving her with him, nor with anybody else. ... I just cry and blame it on myself.”

Eight and a half months pregnant, she said the incident has placed significant strain on her. Asked whether she would rather not have known about the assault, she replied, “Yes, I could have lived without knowing it.”

A former girlfriend of Stiles said that, before his arrest, she lived in fear after contacting police to identify him as the suspect when she saw enhanced images from the videotape on local news.

“I’ve had my share of nightmares,” Elaine Thomas told CNN’s Nancy Grace.

Thomas said she screamed when she recognized the images on television and felt she had no choice but to notify police about the man she had believed was a “weapons enthusiast” with only a minor criminal record.

“How could I not tell them who that man was? That little girl suffered unimaginable things, and I knew for a fact it was him,” Thomas said.

Another former girlfriend of Stiles, Tina Allen, said this month that she believes she is the reason Stiles came into contact with the girl and that she is “mortified” by the allegations against him.

“He said he’d been in the Navy and, you know, I was looking for a strong guy to represent to my sons what I thought they needed to be,” Allen said.

Allen said she took Stiles to a crowded apartment where her son and daughter lived. Also living in the apartment were a family friend and her daughter, the alleged assault victim.

Todd Allen, Tina Allen’s son, said he recognized his former apartment from scenes in the video.

CNN’s Ed Payne and Ted Rowlands contributed to this report.
